July, 2023

Author: Pankaj Bhatia
Bench: Pankaj Bhatia
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench

Court No. - 11
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 9216 of 2023
Applicant :- Umar Ali

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.

Counsel for Applicant :- Upendra Prakash Pathak Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
2. The FIR in question was lodged alleging that the sister of the informant was being harassed by the matrimonial family including the applicant.
On 26.12.2022, the entire family caused physical injury to the sister of the informant and threw out from the house and also stated that she should go and die by jumping in river.
Ultimately, his sister jumped in a river and died.

3. The Counsel for the applicant draws my attention to the subsequent application of the informant given on 24.05.2023 wherein he has stated that the name of the family members was wrongly Umar Ali vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.

entities.text: Umar Ali vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178418460/
1 written as they were not guilty.
He further argues that the applicant is 75 years of age and is father-in-law of the deceased.
He argues that general allegations have been levelled against all the accused persons.
The applicant is in custody since 25.05.2023 and has no criminal antecedents.

4. Learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the bail prayer by arguing that the statements of the neighbours were recorded, who stated that the victim was ill treated, as such, the bail application should be rejected.

5. Considering the averments made in the FIR, the statements of the informant and witnesses,
which do not record that immediately prior to the death of the deceased, anything was done for abetment as defined under Section 107 IPC and also considering the law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Ramesh Kumar vs State; (2009) 1 SCC 618 and M. Arjunan Vs. State,
Represented by its Inspector of Police; (2019) 3 SCC 315 coupled with the fact that the applicant is 75 years old and is in custody since 25.05.2023 and there is nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicant if enlarged on bail, would in any way adversely affect the trial and without expressing any opinion on merit, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
6.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

7. Let the applicant Umar Ali be released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No.464 of 2022, under Sections 34, 498A, 323, 506, 306 IPC, Police Station Dariyabad, District Barabanki on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
Order Date :- 21.7.2023 akverma  Umar Ali vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.
